entire enable
entire brain setup

Enable Entire with session tracking for your AI agent workflows.

If Entire is not yet configured, this runs the full configuration flow.
If Entire is already configured but disabled, this re-enables it.

for you and (optionally) create a matching GitHub repository via the gh CLI.

Usage:
  entire enable [flags]

Flags:
      --absolute-git-hook-path               Embed full binary path in git hooks (for GUI git clients that don't source shell profiles)
      --agent string                         Agent to set up hooks for (e.g., claude-code, codex, copilot-cli, cursor, factoryai-droid, gemini, opencode, pi; external agents on $PATH are also available). Enables non-interactive mode.

      --checkpoint-remote string             Checkpoint remote in provider:owner/repo format (e.g., github:org/checkpoints-repo)
  -f, --force                                Force reinstall hooks (removes existing Entire hooks first)
  -h, --help                                 help for enable
      --import-history                       During first-time setup, import the selected agents' existing session history (last 30 days) without prompting
      --init-repo                            If not a git repo, initialize one non-interactively
      --initial-commit-message string        Commit message for the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --local                                Write settings to .entire/settings.local.json instead of .entire/settings.json
      --no-github                            Initialize local git repo only; skip creating a GitHub remote
      --no-init-repo                         If not a git repo, exit instead of prompting to initialize one
      --project                              Write settings to .entire/settings.json even if it already exists
      --push                                 When bootstrapping a new repo, push the initial commit to the created GitHub remote (implies creating the remote; without it the repo is created but not pushed)

content.content:
---
entire-brain is an external-command plugin for the Entire CLI.

It builds a local, inspectable repository brain from retained sessions, seed
context, docs, history, semantic records, and durable facts, then exposes
retrieval, verification, evaluation, and MCP surfaces for agents.

Usage:
  entire-brain [flags]
  entire-brain [command]

Set up the brain & agents:
  setup          Build the brain and start background updates
  add            Clone a repository, fetch its Entire history, and build its brain
  init-agents    Install coordinated agent instructions
  agent-guide    Preview repository-specific agent instructions
  mcp            Serve local brain tools over MCP stdio
  config         Inspect or initialize plugin configuration

Search & explore the brain:
  overview       Summarize the project, its structure, and decisions
  brief          Gather relevant context for a task
  query          Search the brain (hybrid by default)
  get            Fetch a brain item by ID
  multi-get      Fetch multiple brain items by ID
  dash           Browse the brain in an interactive dashboard

Durable facts & patterns:
  recall         Retrieve durable facts matching a query for the current branch
  remember       Record a durable fact about this repository
  distill        Extract durable facts from sessions (requires an agent)
  facts          Review, promote, and garbage-collect durable facts
  verify         Verify durable fact anchors against local retained sources
  patterns       Inspect and rebuild recurring patterns from sessions

Sessions & conversation memory:
  memory         Manage conversation indexing and background jobs
  privacy        Control which captured sessions the brain retains

Code & semantic index:
  inspect        Explore code, dependencies, and change history
0.1.0
see 'entire plugin search' and 'entire plugin index update'.
  upgrade     Upgrade remote-installed plugins to their newest tag

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, others) working in this repo.

## What this is

Our entry for the Lio challenge "Keep the Line Running" at START Hack Munich 2026.

- Fictional customer: Soony, a games publisher launching Grand Heist 6 on Sun 22 Nov, 20:00
- Everything is packed in one distribution center in Hamburg; six suppliers deliver the parts
- Still open at kickoff: 128,000 Standard Editions (4 parts each) and 25,200 numbered Collector's Editions (7 parts each)
- Packing time left: Sat 06:00 to 22:00, Sun 06:00 to 20:00

The product idea is not fixed yet. Check the README and recent commits for the current direction.

## The rules that shape the code

- **Agents do real work.** They read, decide and act: write to suppliers, open decisions, escalate. A dashboard on top of a spreadsheet is not enough.
- **Nothing hardcoded.** Never copy values from the data into code. Everything is derived from the portal data at runtime.
- **The data changes.** New files land in the portal during the hack, unannounced. Code must handle new and changed files without a rebuild.
- **The data is messy on purpose.** Expect contradictions, missing values, scans and four languages (KR, CN, PL, EN). Surface contradictions instead of silently picking one side.
- **Confidential.** Use the data only for this hackathon and never share it outside the team. Do not commit portal data (`data/` is gitignored); fetch it through the API.

## Data access

- Customer portal: `https://start-hack-portal-cxh3crbdaef2f8gt.westeurope-01.azurewebsites.net`
- API (team token from the portal's Settings): `GET /api/v1/files`, `GET /api/v1/files/{path}`, `GET /api/v1/archive.zip`, `GET /api/v1/openapi.json`
- Token and other secrets go in `.env` (gitignored), never in code or commits
- Supplier email only gets answers from sender addresses registered in the portal's Settings

## Deadlines

- **Sun 12:00:** hand-in: deployed prototype, pitch deck, demo video (max 3 min), this repo with a short README
- **Sun 14:00:** live demo, 3 min pitch plus 2 min questions

Prefer working, deployed and demoable over complete. Go deep on one problem.

## Entire (session tracking)

Entire records agent sessions as checkpoints and links them to commits.

- Hooks for Claude Code (`.claude/settings.json`) and Codex (`.codex/hooks.json`) are committed; they do nothing if `entire` is not installed
- Checkpoints upload to this (private) repo on `git push`

### Setup (once per clone)

1. Install the CLI. macOS: `brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire`. Other systems: see https://docs.entire.io/cli/installation
2. Check it runs: `entire --version`
3. In your clone, install the git hooks (they link commits to checkpoints and upload them on push):

   ```bash
   entire enable --agent claude-code --local --telemetry=false
   entire agent add codex    # only if you use Codex
   ```

   `--local` writes your choices to `.entire/settings.local.json`, so the shared `.entire/settings.json` stays unchanged. Drop `--telemetry=false` if you don't mind anonymous usage stats.
4. **Restart your agents:** quit every Claude Code or Codex session that was open in this repo and start a new one. Hooks load when a session starts, so sessions that were already running are not tracked
5. Codex only: in the new session, open `/hooks` and approve the Entire hooks
6. Verify: `entire status` should show `Enabled`, your agents, `Checkpoints sync to: origin` and `Secret scanners · betterleaks, goredact`
7. If `entire enable` changed `.claude/settings.json` or `.codex/hooks.json`, check `git diff` before committing; the committed versions already work for everyone

`entire doctor` diagnoses and fixes stuck sessions.
- Shared redaction settings (PII, betterleaks, goredact) live in `.entire/settings.json`; personal settings go in `.entire/settings.local.json` (gitignored)
- Redaction is best effort: never paste secrets into agent sessions

## Conventions

- Commit subjects in imperative mood, at most 50 characters; details as bullets in the body
- One commit per topic
- Keep secrets, tokens and personal data out of code, fixtures and commit messages

Entire and the brain are both set up and connected for this repo now.

**Your teammate's push:** 7 new commits on `main`. They set up Entire for the team: shared hooks for Claude Code and Codex, two Entire skills, `.entire/settings.json` with secret redaction, a `.gitignore`, a longer README, and an `AGENTS.md`. AGENTS.md describes the START Hack "Keep the Line Running" challenge (the Soony / Grand Heist 6 packing scenario), the rules for the data, how to get it through the portal API, the Sunday deadlines (hand-in at 12:00, demo at 14:00) and Entire setup steps. I pulled it with a fast-forward.

**What I did:**
- I deleted the Entire config files my first `entire enable` had generated, because they clashed with the committed ones. Then I re-ran `entire enable --agent claude-code --local --telemetry=false` as AGENTS.md says, and reverted the hook changes it made, so the team's committed versions stay as they are.

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, others) working in this repo.

## What this is

Our entry for the Lio challenge "Keep the Line Running" at START Hack Munich 2026.

- Fictional customer: Soony, a games publisher launching Grand Heist 6 on Sun 22 Nov, 20:00
- Everything is packed in one distribution center in Hamburg; six suppliers deliver the parts
- Still open at kickoff: 128,000 Standard Editions (4 parts each) and 25,200 numbered Collector's Editions (7 parts each)
- Packing time left: Sat 06:00 to 22:00, Sun 06:00 to 20:00

The product idea is not fixed yet. Check the README and recent commits for the current direction.

## The rules that shape the code

- **Agents do real work.** They read, decide and act: write to suppliers, open decisions, escalate. A dashboard on top of a spreadsheet is not enough.
- **Nothing hardcoded.** Never copy values from the data into code. Everything is derived from the portal data at runtime.
- **The data changes.** New files land in the portal during the hack, unannounced. Code must handle new and changed files without a rebuild.
- **The data is messy on purpose.** Expect contradictions, missing values, scans and four languages (KR, CN, PL, EN). Surface contradictions instead of silently picking one side.
- **Confidential.** Use the data only for this hackathon and never share it outside the team. Do not commit portal data (`data/` is gitignored); fetch it through the API.

## Data access

- Customer portal: `https://start-hack-portal-cxh3crbdaef2f8gt.westeurope-01.azurewebsites.net`
- API (team token from the portal's Settings): `GET /api/v1/files`, `GET /api/v1/files/{path}`, `GET /api/v1/archive.zip`, `GET /api/v1/openapi.json`
- Token and other secrets go in `.env` (gitignored), never in code or commits
- Supplier email only gets answers from sender addresses registered in the portal's Settings

## Deadlines

- **Sun 12:00:** hand-in: deployed prototype, pitch deck, demo video (max 3 min), this repo with a short README
- **Sun 14:00:** live demo, 3 min pitch plus 2 min questions

Prefer working, deployed and demoable over complete. Go deep on one problem.

## Entire (session tracking)

Entire records agent sessions as checkpoints and links them to commits.

- Hooks for Claude Code (`.claude/settings.json`) and Codex (`.codex/hooks.json`) are committed; they do nothing if `entire` is not installed
- Checkpoints upload to this (private) repo on `git push`

### Setup (once per clone)

1. Install the CLI. macOS: `brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire`. Other systems: see https://docs.entire.io/cli/installation
2. Check it runs: `entire --version`
3. In your clone, install the git hooks (they link commits to checkpoints and upload them on push):

   ```bash
   entire enable --agent claude-code --local --telemetry=false
   entire agent add codex    # only if you use Codex
   ```

   `--local` writes your choices to `.entire/settings.local.json`, so the shared `.entire/settings.json` stays unchanged. Drop `--telemetry=false` if you don't mind anonymous usage stats.
4. **Restart your agents:** quit every Claude Code or Codex session that was open in this repo and start a new one. Hooks load when a session starts, so sessions that were already running are not tracked
5. Codex only: in the new session, open `/hooks` and approve the Entire hooks
6. Verify: `entire status` should show `Enabled`, your agents, `Checkpoints sync to: origin` and `Secret scanners · betterleaks, goredact`
7. If `entire enable` changed `.claude/settings.json` or `.codex/hooks.json`, check `git diff` before committing; the committed versions already work for everyone

`entire doctor` diagnoses and fixes stuck sessions.
- Shared redaction settings (PII, betterleaks, goredact) live in `.entire/settings.json`; personal settings go in `.entire/settings.local.json` (gitignored)
- Redaction is best effort: never paste secrets into agent sessions

## Conventions

- Commit subjects in imperative mood, at most 50 characters; details as bullets in the body
- One commit per topic
- Keep secrets, tokens and personal data out of code, fixtures and commit messages

This beats GitHub Issues for a weekend hackathon because it costs nothing to set up and agents follow it automatically. The cost is that a shared file can get merge conflicts when two people edit it at once. One line per person keeps them small.

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, others) working in this repo.

## What this is

Our entry for the Lio challenge "Keep the Line Running" at START Hack Munich 2026.

- Fictional customer: Soony, a games publisher launching Grand Heist 6 on Sun 22 Nov, 20:00
- Everything is packed in one distribution center in Hamburg; six suppliers deliver the parts
- Still open at kickoff: 128,000 Standard Editions (4 parts each) and 25,200 numbered Collector's Editions (7 parts each)
- Packing time left: Sat 06:00 to 22:00, Sun 06:00 to 20:00

The product idea is not fixed yet. Check the README and recent commits for the current direction.

## The rules that shape the code

- **Agents do real work.** They read, decide and act: write to suppliers, open decisions, escalate. A dashboard on top of a spreadsheet is not enough.
- **Nothing hardcoded.** Never copy values from the data into code. Everything is derived from the portal data at runtime.
- **The data changes.** New files land in the portal during the hack, unannounced. Code must handle new and changed files without a rebuild.
- **The data is messy on purpose.** Expect contradictions, missing values, scans and four languages (KR, CN, PL, EN). Surface contradictions instead of silently picking one side.
- **Confidential.** Use the data only for this hackathon and never share it outside the team. Do not commit portal data (`data/` is gitignored); fetch it through the API.

## Data access

- Customer portal: `https://start-hack-portal-cxh3crbdaef2f8gt.westeurope-01.azurewebsites.net`
- API (team token from the portal's Settings): `GET /api/v1/files`, `GET /api/v1/files/{path}`, `GET /api/v1/archive.zip`, `GET /api/v1/openapi.json`
- Token and other secrets go in `.env` (gitignored), never in code or commits
- Supplier email only gets answers from sender addresses registered in the portal's Settings

## Deadlines

- **Sun 12:00:** hand-in: deployed prototype, pitch deck, demo video (max 3 min), this repo with a short README
- **Sun 14:00:** live demo, 3 min pitch plus 2 min questions

Prefer working, deployed and demoable over complete. Go deep on one problem.

## Entire (session tracking)

Entire records agent sessions as checkpoints and links them to commits.

- Hooks for Claude Code (`.claude/settings.json`) and Codex (`.codex/hooks.json`) are committed; they do nothing if `entire` is not installed
- Checkpoints upload to this (private) repo on `git push`

### Setup (once per clone)

1. Install the CLI. macOS: `brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire`. Other systems: see https://docs.entire.io/cli/installation
2. Check it runs: `entire --version`
3. In your clone, install the git hooks (they link commits to checkpoints and upload them on push):

   ```bash
   entire enable --agent claude-code --local --telemetry=false
   entire agent add codex    # only if you use Codex
   ```

   `--local` writes your choices to `.entire/settings.local.json`, so the shared `.entire/settings.json` stays unchanged. Drop `--telemetry=false` if you don't mind anonymous usage stats.
4. **Restart your agents:** quit every Claude Code or Codex session that was open in this repo and start a new one. Hooks load when a session starts, so sessions that were already running are not tracked
5. Codex only: in the new session, open `/hooks` and approve the Entire hooks
6. Verify: `entire status` should show `Enabled`, your agents, `Checkpoints sync to: origin` and `Secret scanners · betterleaks, goredact`
7. If `entire enable` changed `.claude/settings.json` or `.codex/hooks.json`, check `git diff` before committing; the committed versions already work for everyone

`entire doctor` diagnoses and fixes stuck sessions.
- Shared redaction settings (PII, betterleaks, goredact) live in `.entire/settings.json`; personal settings go in `.entire/settings.local.json` (gitignored)
- Redaction is best effort: never paste secrets into agent sessions

## Entire Brain (shared team memory)

Brain distills agent sessions into durable memories and syncs them across the team. Agents read `.entire/agent-guide.md` (linked from `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`) for how to use it.

### Setup (once per clone, after the Entire setup above)

1. The CLI must be 0.11.6 or newer: `entire --version`. Upgrade with `brew upgrade --cask entire`. If an older `entire` sits earlier on your `PATH` (e.g. `~/.local/bin`), remove it
2. Install the plugins:

   ```bash
   entire plugin install brain
   entire plugin install graph
   ```

3. In your clone, build the brain and connect it to the team's hosted memory set:

   ```bash
   entire brain setup
   entire brain connect
   ```

   `setup` also installs a background watcher that refreshes the brain every 5 minutes. It refuses to index a dirty working tree, so commit or stash first
4. Restart your agents, as above
5. Verify: `entire brain status` should show `Daemon | running` and `Brainstore | connected`
6. If `entire brain setup` changed `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/settings.json`, check `git diff`; the committed versions already work for everyone

## Conventions

- Commit subjects in imperative mood, at most 50 characters; details as bullets in the body
- One commit per topic
- Keep secrets, tokens and personal data out of code, fixtures and commit messages

# Claude in Chrome

Claude in Chrome is a browser extension. Its tools, named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`, act in the person's real Chrome, in new tabs alongside the person's own, with their existing sign-ins. Claude in Chrome is available only while the person's Chrome is running with the extension connected; if its tool calls report that the extension is not connected or get no response, Claude says so rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

If the only Claude in Chrome tool present is `enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome`, Claude calls it first: it turns Claude in Chrome on for this conversation, and the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools appear once it has run.

## Loading the tools

If the `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools are deferred (meaning they have to be loaded through ToolSearch before use), Claude loads every tool it expects to need in ONE ToolSearch call, because the select query accepts a comma-separated list and each extra ToolSearch call costs a full round trip. The core set to start with:

```
ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"
```

Claude adds task-specific tools to that same call when the task obviously needs them: `read_console_messages` and `read_network_requests` for debugging, `form_input` for forms, `gif_creator` for recordings, `javascript_tool` for page scripting. A second ToolSearch is only for a tool the task turned out to need later.

## Starting a session: tab context first, then a new tab

At the start of each browser session Claude calls `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp` first, to see the person's current tabs and understand what they may want to work with. Then:

1. Claude reuses an existing tab only when the person explicitly asks to work with it.
2. Otherwise Claude opens a new tab with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp` and works there, and, unless the person wants them kept, closes the tabs it created before finishing.
3. Claude never reuses tab IDs remembered from an earlier or different session. If a tool reports that a tab does not exist or is invalid, or the person closes a tab, or a navigation error occurs, Claude calls `tabs_context_mcp` again for fresh tab IDs.

## Site permissions

Claude in Chrome acts on a site only once the person has allowed it; depending on their settings the person may be prompted per site, in the extension or in the app. When a tool call is waiting on or refused that permission, Claude tells the person and waits for them to allow it rather than working around it. A site the person declines is their decision; Claude moves on.

## Recording a GIF

For multi-step interactions the person may want to review or share, Claude can record them with `mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator`. Claude captures a few extra frames before and after each action so playback is smooth, and gives the file a meaningful name (for example "login_process.gif").

## Reading console output

`mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages` reads the page's console. Console output can be verbose, so when Claude is looking for specific entries it passes the `pattern` parameter (a regular expression), for example pattern "[MyApp]" to keep only the application's own logs.

## Alerts and dialogs

Claude does not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or other browser modal dialogs through its actions. Those dialogs block all further browser events, so the extension stops receiving commands. Instead:

1. Claude avoids clicking elements likely to raise a confirmation dialog (for example a "Delete" button) unless necessary.
2. If it must interact with such an element, Claude warns the person first that this may interrupt the session.
3. Claude can use `mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool` to check for and dismiss an existing dialog before proceeding, and prefers `console.log` plus `read_console_messages` over `alert` for debugging.

If a dialog does get triggered and the browser stops responding, Claude tells the person they need to dismiss it manually in Chrome.

## Staying on task, and when to stop

Claude stays focused on the specific task and does not wander into unrelated pages. Claude stops and asks the person how to proceed, explaining what it tried and what went wrong, when any of these happen:

- browser tool calls fail or return errors after 2 or 3 attempts
- the extension gives no response
- page elements do not respond to clicks or input, or pages do not load or time out
- the task turns out to involve unexpected complexity or tangents
- several approaches have not completed the task

Claude does not keep retrying the same failing action.

The API can't read the mail, so the options all depend on the web app. The portal API only lists and downloads files; I tried `/emails`, `/inbox`, `/messages` and `/mail`, and all return 404. The web app at `/app` sits behind a sign-in page that asks for your team name and password.

Here's what we can do, best first:

1. **Connect Claude in Chrome (recommended).** Open Chrome with the Claude extension installed, make sure it's signed in to the same claude.ai account as Claude Code, and sign in to the portal yourself. Then I can open the inbox in a new tab, read it now, and come back to check it whenever you ask. If it still says "not connected", restarting Chrome usually fixes it.
2. **Paste the email into chat.** This is the quickest option for a single email, but you'd have to do it for every new one.
3. **Check your own mailbox.** If the email went to your personal email inbox rather than the portal, I don't have a mail connector in this session. Either connect one or paste the email.

I can't type the portal password for you, even in a headless browser, so option 1 relies on you being signed in already in your own Chrome.

There are no emails in the data. The newest messages are two supplier notices from **Karton Nowak** (SUP-0028, a printer in Poznań). The portal still has the same 308 files we downloaded and nothing new has arrived, so if a real email came in, it's in the portal inbox or your own mailbox, not the files.

**1. Rush offer, dated 21 Nov and valid for 24 hours** (`Oferta_tryb_ekspresowy_2026-11-21.pdf`)
- **Rush printing:** up to 50,000 sleeves, leaflets or posters, ready 36 hours after they get a print-ready file, at their price list plus 35%.
- **Art books:** 8,000 spare Grand Heist 6 Art Books (`CMP-GAM-008`) already in their warehouse, loaded within 4 hours of an order, at list price.
- **Transport:** the truck from Poznań to Hamburg takes about 9 hours.

**2. Downtime notice, dated 9 Nov** (`Zawiadomienie_przestoj_techniczny_2026-11.pdf`, in Polish)
- The offset press and the hardcover binding line are both down from **21 Nov 14:00 until 23 Nov 06:00**.
- During the downtime, rush jobs run only on the digital line, which handles at most **15,000** pieces per 36 hours.
- The cut-off for rush jobs on the offset press was **21 Nov 09:00**, which has already passed.
- Shipping finished goods from their warehouse is still possible.

**These two notices contradict each other.** The offer promises 50,000 rush pieces, but the downtime notice caps it at 15,000, and the offer itself asks you to take the downtime into account. The real options are:
- the **8,000 art books** in stock, which can ship now: 4 hours to load plus 9 hours on the road gets them to Hamburg around Sunday morning if ordered soon;
- up to **15,000** printed pieces, which would only be ready about 36 hours after the file is sent. That would be cutting it close to the Sunday 20:00 deadline.

The background agent will place this against the bill of materials and the shortfall in its write-up.

content.text:
Git had nothing new; your teammate hasn't pushed since `4d1e0bd`. The portal did have new data: 5 new files and 1 changed file, posted Saturday around 14:00. I downloaded all six and added a summary to the end of `data/UNDERSTANDING.md`.

**What changed:**
- **CPO memo on launch priorities:** Collector's Editions get any short part first, including game cards. Nothing ships with a part Quality hasn't released, and Quality has the final say. Air freight or rush orders above the approval limits must reach the CPO within the hour, with the cost set against the copies gained. Management wants one page a day on what could stop a line, "not forty dashboards", which fits the war-room idea well.
- **Sleeves:** an engineering change makes artwork rev C the valid one and says rev B "must not be packed". That settles the sleeve question in favour of Nowak's rev C sleeves. PackRight's rev B sleeves now have to be blocked from packing.
- **Poster:** moves to rev B, but rev A stock can still be used up, so no impact.
- **Statues:** now marked as a critical part. That makes the 5,600 statues that failed inspection even harder to use.
- **Org chart v2:** the Collector's Category Lead (Arjun Krishnan) only starts on Monday 23 Nov. The post stays vacant over the weekend, so the statue decision still goes to Dr. Maren Vogt.
- **Launch status as of Saturday 13:00:**

  | Edition | Packed | Still to pack | Rate |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Standard | 554,000 | 86,000 | 6,000/hour |
  | Collector's | 53,100 | 18,900 | 900/hour |

  Collector's needs about 21 of the roughly 23 shift hours left, so very little slack.
- **`products.csv` changed format:** two columns were renamed or added, including a new day-one quantity. The day-one figure for Standard is 640,000, which contradicts the roughly 415,000 pre-orders the earlier analysis found.

Two things follow for the build:
- The portal really does drop new files without notice, so whatever we build needs to check for new files regularly.
- Parsers will break when columns get renamed, as `products.csv` just showed.

# Lio Challenge: "Keep the Line Running" (START Hack Munich 2026)

This file is the complete challenge context, compiled from the four official documents Lio provided: the challenge brief, the judging criteria, the deep-dive slides (including speaker notes) and a challenge summary. It describes the problem only. It contains no proposed solution or architecture. Those decisions are open.

> Soony, Popstar Studios and Grand Heist 6 are entirely fictional.
> Use the challenge data only for this hackathon and do not share it outside the team.

---

## 1. Role and framing

- The team plays **Lio**, a young AI startup that has just closed its **first paying customer, Soony**.
- Lio (the real company) runs procurement end to end for 175+ global enterprises (BMW, Siemens, ZEISS, among others) with a multi-agent system of hundreds of specialised AI agents.
- Soony bought "an AI solution to save the launch." **That solution does not exist yet. The team has to build it.**
- Why Soony bought a startup: no time for a tender or a big vendor project. They needed help this weekend. The last three weeks nearly broke their team.
- Sales call: the CPO asked, "Can it chase suppliers for us?" The answer was, "Yes, sort of." The pitch was "an AI workforce that keeps their supply chain running."
- **Soony's ask: "No more surprises."**
- Soony's stated pain: "Suppliers tell us about problems way too late. By then, our launch date is already at risk, and every fix is expensive."
- Quote from Soony: "Our fans have waited years for this game. If it is not on the shelf on Sunday, nobody will remember the game. They will remember that we missed it."

---

## 2. The customer: Soony Interactive GmbH

- A console and games publisher headquartered in **Munich**.
- Releasing **Grand Heist 6**, developed by Popstar Studios. The heist series is back after 13 years. It's the biggest game release of the year.
- **Soony makes nothing itself.** Six suppliers deliver the parts, and every copy is packed at **one site: Soony's distribution center in Hamburg**. There is **no plan B site**.
- From Hamburg, trucks take the boxes to retailers across Europe.

### Key facts

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Launch | **Sunday 22 November 2026, 20:00**. The date cannot move: it's fixed by retail and by pre-orders |
| Trucks to retail | Leave Hamburg from Sunday 20:00. **Whatever is not on them misses launch day** |
| Pre-orders | 487,000 |
| Standard Edition demand (day one) | 640,000 copies |
| Collector's Edition demand | 72,000 copies, **every copy numbered, all pre-ordered** |
| Suppliers | 6 |
| Logistics providers | 4 (ocean, air cargo, a forwarder in India, trucks from Poznań) |
| Distribution center | 1, in Hamburg |
| Packing time left | **30 hours**: Sat 06:00–22:00 and Sun 06:00–20:00. **No night shift** |
| Why so late | The game master was finished late, so the programmed game cards only started arriving three weeks ago |

---

## 3. Situation at kickoff: "80% packed, the last 20% is on you"

| | Standard Edition | Collector's Edition |
|---|---|---|
| Packed at kickoff | 512,000 of 640,000 (80%) | 46,800 of 72,000 (65%) |
| Still to pack | 128,000 | 25,200 |
| Parts per box | 4 | 7 |
| Packing setup | 3 pack lines | 1 manual cell; **all 7 parts must be present at the same time** |
| Hours needed (of 30 left) | 21 | 28 |
| Slack | 9 hours | **2 hours** |
| Rate (derived) | ~6,100 copies/hour | **900 copies/hour; every hour the cell waits for a part costs 900 copies** |

Additional facts:
- **Standard Edition parts:** game card, clear case, cover sleeve, activation code leaflet.
- **Collector's Edition parts:** game card, steel case, collector's box, art book, city map poster, die-cast statue, leaflet.
- The Standard pack lines are **not exclusively reserved** for the launch: Grand Heist 5 reprints still run on the side.
- Standard "is not where the launch breaks, as long as the game cards keep coming."
- Collector's Edition: fans paid for a specific numbered copy, so Soony **cannot ship fewer or swap them**. If one part is missing (e.g. the statue or the art book), the whole cell stands still. Lio calls the Collector's Edition "the real risk this weekend."
- The first 80% took three weeks of firefighting: chasing suppliers by phone, rebooking freight, packing whatever arrived that day. The team is exhausted. The last 20% has no buffer.
- Soony's fear: something in the last 20% blows up and nobody notices until Sunday.
- **Hint from the brief:** "The system says we are fine. My gut says we are not." (*Somebody at Soony, probably. Find out who is right.*)

---

## 4. Supply network

All parts end up in the Hamburg distribution center.

| Supplier | Country | Supplies | Route / transit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hwaseong Memory | South Korea | **70% of game cards** | Sea via Busan (36 days) or air via Incheon |
| Boise Semi | USA | **30% of game cards** | Air via Chicago |
| Guangzhou PackRight | China | Card cases, sleeves, collector's boxes | Sea from Yantian |
| Dongguan Precision Housings | China | Steel cases, **80% of statues**, card cases | Sea from Yantian |

This file is the complete challenge context, compiled from the four official documents Lio provided: the challenge brief, the judging criteria, the deep-dive slides (including speaker notes) and a challenge summary. It describes the problem only. It contains no proposed solution or architecture. Those decisions are open.

> Soony, Popstar Studios and Grand Heist 6 are entirely fictional.
> Use the challenge data only for this hackathon and do not share it outside the team.

---

## 1. Role and framing

- The team plays **Lio**, a young AI startup that has just closed its **first paying customer, Soony**.
- Lio (the real company) runs procurement end to end for 175+ global enterprises (BMW, Siemens, ZEISS, among others) with a multi-agent system of hundreds of specialised AI agents.
- Soony bought "an AI solution to save the launch." **That solution does not exist yet. The team has to build it.**
- Why Soony bought a startup: no time for a tender or a big vendor project. They needed help this weekend. The last three weeks nearly broke their team.
- Sales call: the CPO asked, "Can it chase suppliers for us?" The answer was, "Yes, sort of." The pitch was "an AI workforce that keeps their supply chain running."
- **Soony's ask: "No more surprises."**
- Soony's stated pain: "Suppliers tell us about problems way too late. By then, our launch date is already at risk, and every fix is expensive."
- Quote from Soony: "Our fans have waited years for this game. If it is not on the shelf on Sunday, nobody will remember the game. They will remember that we missed it."

---

## 2. The customer: Soony Interactive GmbH

- A console and games publisher headquartered in **Munich**.
- Releasing **Grand Heist 6**, developed by Popstar Studios. The heist series is back after 13 years. It's the biggest game release of the year.
- **Soony makes nothing itself.** Six suppliers deliver the parts, and every copy is packed at **one site: Soony's distribution center in Hamburg**. There is **no plan B site**.
- From Hamburg, trucks take the boxes to retailers across Europe.

### Key facts

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Launch | **Sunday 22 November 2026, 20:00**. The date cannot move: it's fixed by retail and by pre-orders |
| Trucks to retail | Leave Hamburg from Sunday 20:00. **Whatever is not on them misses launch day** |
| Pre-orders | 487,000 |
| Standard Edition demand (day one) | 640,000 copies |
| Collector's Edition demand | 72,000 copies, **every copy numbered, all pre-ordered** |
| Suppliers | 6 |
| Logistics providers | 4 (ocean, air cargo, a forwarder in India, trucks from Poznań) |
| Distribution center | 1, in Hamburg |
| Packing time left | **30 hours**: Sat 06:00–22:00 and Sun 06:00–20:00. **No night shift** |
| Why so late | The game master was finished late, so the programmed game cards only started arriving three weeks ago |

---

## 3. Situation at kickoff: "80% packed, the last 20% is on you"

| | Standard Edition | Collector's Edition |
|---|---|---|
| Packed at kickoff | 512,000 of 640,000 (80%) | 46,800 of 72,000 (65%) |
| Still to pack | 128,000 | 25,200 |
| Parts per box | 4 | 7 |
| Packing setup | 3 pack lines | 1 manual cell; **all 7 parts must be present at the same time** |
| Hours needed (of 30 left) | 21 | 28 |
| Slack | 9 hours | **2 hours** |
| Rate (derived) | ~6,100 copies/hour | **900 copies/hour; every hour the cell waits for a part costs 900 copies** |

Additional facts:
- **Standard Edition parts:** game card, clear case, cover sleeve, activation code leaflet.
- **Collector's Edition parts:** game card, steel case, collector's box, art book, city map poster, die-cast statue, leaflet.
- The Standard pack lines are **not exclusively reserved** for the launch: Grand Heist 5 reprints still run on the side.
- Standard "is not where the launch breaks, as long as the game cards keep coming."
- Collector's Edition: fans paid for a specific numbered copy, so Soony **cannot ship fewer or swap them**. If one part is missing (e.g. the statue or the art book), the whole cell stands still. Lio calls the Collector's Edition "the real risk this weekend."
- The first 80% took three weeks of firefighting: chasing suppliers by phone, rebooking freight, packing whatever arrived that day. The team is exhausted. The last 20% has no buffer.
- Soony's fear: something in the last 20% blows up and nobody notices until Sunday.
- **Hint from the brief:** "The system says we are fine. My gut says we are not." (*Somebody at Soony, probably. Find out who is right.*)

---

## 4. Supply network

All parts end up in the Hamburg distribution center.

| Supplier | Country | Supplies | Route / transit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hwaseong Memory | South Korea | **70% of game cards** | Sea via Busan (36 days) or air via Incheon |
| Boise Semi | USA | **30% of game cards** | Air via Chicago |
| Guangzhou PackRight | China | Card cases, sleeves, collector's boxes | Sea from Yantian |
| Dongguan Precision Housings | China | Steel cases, **80% of statues**, card cases | Sea from Yantian |
| Pune Diecast Works | India | **20% of statues**; new supplier since August | Sea from Nhava Sheva, via a forwarder |
| Karton Nowak | Poland | Sleeves, art book, poster, leaflets | Truck from Poznań, one truck day |

From Lio's speaker notes:
- "Anything ordered from Asia today arrives after the launch."
- "The only supplier that can still deliver before Sunday is Karton Nowak."
- "Everything else that will save this launch is already on a ship, on a plane, at a terminal or in the warehouse."
- Brief: "What is ordered now will mostly arrive too late."

---

## 5. Process: how a part gets into the box

| # | Step | Where it lives | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Order | **SAP** (system of record) | Felix, the senior buyer, raises a purchase order |
| 2 | Confirm | Email, PDF | Supplier confirms in its own language and format |
| 3 | Ship | 4 logistics providers | Sea, air or truck |
| 4 | Track | Spreadsheet | ~20 open shipments, hand-kept, updated "when someone remembers" |
| 5 | Receive | Paper scans | Hamburg checks the delivery note, books the goods receipt, stocks the parts |
| 6 | Pack | **Pack-out log** (system of record) | Standard on 3 lines; Collector's in 1 manual cell |
| 7 | Sell | Sun 20:00 | Retail plus 487,000 pre-orders |

- **Only 2 of 7 steps have a system.** Everything in between runs on email, PDFs, scans and phone calls.
- Once the order leaves Soony and goes to the supplier, **Soony is blind until the truck shows up in Hamburg**. Lio: "That gap is where surprises are born, and that gap is where your agents can do real work."
- Head of Procurement: **"We find out at the dock."**
- Suppliers write in their own language: **Korean, Chinese, Polish, English**.
- On the data, Soony says: **"It is what it is."**

Kickoff w/ Soony – notes (11 Nov)

- launch: Sun 22 Nov, 20:00. 487k pre-orders. date cannot move.
- SAP has the purchase orders. nothing else. rest = Excel, PDFs, paper
- suppliers write in their own language: KR, CN, PL, EN
- ~20 open shipments in a spreadsheet, updated "when someone remembers"
- head of procurement: "We find out at the dock."
- why us: suppliers flag problems too late. launch at risk, every fix expensive
- on the data: "It is what it is."
- first demo: Sunday (!!)

| Collector's Edition demand | 72,000 copies, **every copy numbered, all pre-ordered** |
| Suppliers | 6 |
| Logistics providers | 4 (ocean, air cargo, a forwarder in India, trucks from Poznań) |
| Distribution center | 1, in Hamburg |
| Packing time left | **30 hours**: Sat 06:00–22:00 and Sun 06:00–20:00. **No night shift** |
| Why so late | The game master was finished late, so the programmed game cards only started arriving three weeks ago |

---

## 3. Situation at kickoff: "80% packed, the last 20% is on you"

| | Standard Edition | Collector's Edition |
|---|---|---|
| Packed at kickoff | 512,000 of 640,000 (80%) | 46,800 of 72,000 (65%) |
| Still to pack | 128,000 | 25,200 |
| Parts per box | 4 | 7 |
| Packing setup | 3 pack lines | 1 manual cell; **all 7 parts must be present at the same time** |
| Hours needed (of 30 left) | 21 | 28 |
| Slack | 9 hours | **2 hours** |
| Rate (derived) | ~6,100 copies/hour | **900 copies/hour; every hour the cell waits for a part costs 900 copies** |

Additional facts:
- **Standard Edition parts:** game card, clear case, cover sleeve, activation code leaflet.
- **Collector's Edition parts:** game card, steel case, collector's box, art book, city map poster, die-cast statue, leaflet.
- The Standard pack lines are **not exclusively reserved** for the launch: Grand Heist 5 reprints still run on the side.
- Standard "is not where the launch breaks, as long as the game cards keep coming."
- Collector's Edition: fans paid for a specific numbered copy, so Soony **cannot ship fewer or swap them**. If one part is missing (e.g. the statue or the art book), the whole cell stands still. Lio calls the Collector's Edition "the real risk this weekend."
- The first 80% took three weeks of firefighting: chasing suppliers by phone, rebooking freight, packing whatever arrived that day. The team is exhausted. The last 20% has no buffer.
- Soony's fear: something in the last 20% blows up and nobody notices until Sunday.
- **Hint from the brief:** "The system says we are fine. My gut says we are not." (*Somebody at Soony, probably. Find out who is right.*)

---

## 4. Supply network

All parts end up in the Hamburg distribution center.

| Supplier | Country | Supplies | Route / transit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hwaseong Memory | South Korea | **70% of game cards** | Sea via Busan (36 days) or air via Incheon |
| Boise Semi | USA | **30% of game cards** | Air via Chicago |
| Guangzhou PackRight | China | Card cases, sleeves, collector's boxes | Sea from Yantian |
| Dongguan Precision Housings | China | Steel cases, **80% of statues**, card cases | Sea from Yantian |
| Pune Diecast Works | India | **20% of statues**; new supplier since August | Sea from Nhava Sheva, via a forwarder |
| Karton Nowak | Poland | Sleeves, art book, poster, leaflets | Truck from Poznań, one truck day |

From Lio's speaker notes:
- "Anything ordered from Asia today arrives after the launch."
- "The only supplier that can still deliver before Sunday is Karton Nowak."
- "Everything else that will save this launch is already on a ship, on a plane, at a terminal or in the warehouse."
- Brief: "What is ordered now will mostly arrive too late."

---

## 5. Process: how a part gets into the box

| # | Step | Where it lives | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Order | **SAP** (system of record) | Felix, the senior buyer, raises a purchase order |
| 2 | Confirm | Email, PDF | Supplier confirms in its own language and format |
| 3 | Ship | 4 logistics providers | Sea, air or truck |
| 4 | Track | Spreadsheet | ~20 open shipments, hand-kept, updated "when someone remembers" |
| 5 | Receive | Paper scans | Hamburg checks the delivery note, books the goods receipt, stocks the parts |
| 6 | Pack | **Pack-out log** (system of record) | Standard on 3 lines; Collector's in 1 manual cell |
| 7 | Sell | Sun 20:00 | Retail plus 487,000 pre-orders |

- **Only 2 of 7 steps have a system.** Everything in between runs on email, PDFs, scans and phone calls.
- Once the order leaves Soony and goes to the supplier, **Soony is blind until the truck shows up in Hamburg**. Lio: "That gap is where surprises are born, and that gap is where your agents can do real work."
- Head of Procurement: **"We find out at the dock."**
- Suppliers write in their own language: **Korean, Chinese, Polish, English**.
- On the data, Soony says: **"It is what it is."**

### Onboarding notes (in the data as `soony/context/onboarding_notes.md`)

```
Kickoff w/ Soony – notes (11 Nov)

- launch: Sun 22 Nov, 20:00. 487k pre-orders. date cannot move.
- SAP has the purchase orders. nothing else. rest = Excel, PDFs, paper
- suppliers write in their own language: KR, CN, PL, EN
- ~20 open shipments in a spreadsheet, updated "when someone remembers"
- head of procurement: "We find out at the dock."
- why us: suppliers flag problems too late. launch at risk, every fix expensive
- on the data: "It is what it is."
- first demo: Sunday (!!)
```

---

## 6. What can go wrong (Lio's list)

1. A shipment is late, split into several deliveries, or stuck at a port.
2. A supplier delivers the wrong part, the wrong version, or too little.
3. A part is in stock in the system but not on the shelf.
4. A contract or price changes in the small print.
5. Nobody knows who approves the fix.
6. The world happens: strikes, export bans, weather (the summary also mentions geopolitics and earthquakes).

Lio: "This happens every week in every company that buys things. The difference this weekend: there are only 50 hours left. A problem found on Sunday morning is a problem found too late."

---

## 7. The mission

- **Build what was sold.** Lio prescribes no technology, architecture or product idea.
- **The team decides:** the pain point to own, the product, the tech (software, hardware, voice, anything), the business model.
- **The team gets:** a customer with a real problem, their messy data and a world that keeps moving, their suppliers (who write back), and three people from their team to interview.

### THE ONE RULE

> **Agents do real work. Your AI reads, decides and acts (writes, escalates, talks to people). A dashboard on top of a spreadsheet is not enough.**

- "Do not build everything. Nobody saves a launch in 30 hours by fixing everything. Pick the pain that excites you most, one the customer's team tells you about or one nobody has noticed yet, and go deep."
- The jury wants to see the agents work on Soony's real, messy data, and to hear **what they found that Soony's team missed**.
- Do not treat it as a one-off consulting job. Build a scalable product.

### Ten directions from Lio
"Not a checklist. Pick one, combine three, or ignore all of them."

1. **Launch Control Room**: Will we make Sunday 20:00? And what breaks first?
2. **Supplier Chaser**: Agents that ask, confirm and escalate before it is too late.
3. **Stock Truth**: What the system says vs. what is really there.
4. **Plan B**: Something is missing. What can still arrive in time?
5. **Truck & Port Tracker**: Containers, trucks, slots, delays.
6. **Contract Intelligence**: What do the contracts actually say, and who owes whom?
7. **Release Gate**: What may legally and safely go into the box?
8. **Decision Copilot**: A recommendation with a price on it, for a boss with no time.
9. **Supplier-side Tools**: Build for the other side of the table.
10. **Wildcard**: The idea we did not think of.

---

## 8. Toolkit

### Customer portal
- URL: `https://start-hack-portal-cxh3crbdaef2f8gt.westeurope-01.azurewebsites.net`
- **Register** the team, then log in with the team name and password.
- **Data view:** browse the current state folder by folder. New drops show up as a notification, and the page updates by itself.
- **Settings:** the team token for the API, sender addresses for supplier email, office-hour booking.
- Announcements also appear on the portal dashboard and on Discord.

### API
Authenticate with the team token from Settings. The full docs are in the portal, and the exact auth scheme is in the OpenAPI spec.

| Endpoint | Returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/files` | Every file with size, checksum and URL |
| `GET /api/v1/files/{path}` | One file |
| `GET /api/v1/archive.zip` | Everything at once |
| `GET /api/v1/openapi.json` | The OpenAPI spec |

### Data at kickoff
"Realistic, which means it is messy, incomplete and occasionally contradicts itself. **There are things hidden in it that a careful team will find.**" Some shipments are missing from master data or buried in random spreadsheets, and documents come in multiple languages.

| Category | Contents |
|---|---|
| Master data | Products, editions, bills of materials, suppliers, sites |
| Transactions | Purchase orders, goods receipts, stock, shipments |
| Documents | Contracts and supplier documents (order confirmations, notices, scans), in more than one format |
| Context | How Soony's procurement is organised, its policies, the onboarding notes |

### A live, changing world
- New information lands in the portal during the hack, **unannounced**. **Nobody tells you what changed.** "You get files, not explanations."
- The dataset starts relatively small. More data and changes are released step by step.
- "You do not have to react to every drop. Use what helps your product and your story." The agents should notice.
- It's **sleep-friendly**: "Not even Soony works at night."
- Lio advises against hardcoding fixes or overfitting to specific events. It wants a system that handles these kinds of change generally.

Four kinds of drops:

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| Logistics | Shipments and trucks that do not go to plan |
| Suppliers | Messages and documents that change the picture |
| Customer | New requests and rules from Soony |
| News | What happens in the world and touches the launch |

Two illustrative examples from Lio (these exact events won't happen, but similar ones will):
- **Something new appears:** `suppliers/<ID>/notices/bank_details_change.pdf` is added. The IBAN doesn't match the contract. Real change, or invoice fraud?
- **Something stops changing:** in `soony/erp/open_shipments.json`, `updated_at` stops moving and there are no new statuses for 18 hours (the carrier got hacked). "No news isn't good news: nobody knows where those containers are right now."

### Supplier inbox
- All 6 suppliers have real email addresses and **write back**.
- **Register every sender address in Settings first**, including any address the agents send from. Mail from unregistered addresses gets no reply.
- "Where to reach them, and how they react, is yours to find out." "Agent to agent, if you dare."
- Treat them like real business partners. Keep emails concise, professional and targeted. Suppliers who get spammed may get frustrated and stop cooperating.

### Tech
Any stack, language, framework, model or orchestration. Hardware is optional. Lio engineers are at the booth all weekend for technical questions. Questions go to Discord.

---

## 9. Office hours: Soony's project team

Three personas, each played by people from Lio's team. Each knows things that are **not in the data**.

| Persona | Role | Ask about |
|---|---|---|
| **Dr. Maren Vogt** | Head of Procurement (CPO) | Money, priorities, what a missing copy costs, who signs what. "What matters, and what does it cost?" |
| **Felix Brunner** | Senior Buyer | Suppliers, trucks, stock, how things really run (not how the handbook says), the workarounds nobody wrote down |
| **Nils Berger** | IT & Systems Lead | Data, files, exports, systems: "Why does this file look like that?" Precise questions only |

- 3 blocks over the weekend. Times are announced in the portal and on Discord (the deep-dive slides listed Sat 14:00, Sat 17:00, Sun 09:00; the portal showed Block A at Sat 15:00).
- 10 minutes per team and person, booked in the portal. Wishes are ranked and seats drawn by lottery, one talk per block.

How Soony's team behaves:
- They answer what you ask. **They do not volunteer.** Good questions get good answers.
- They're the customer, not a mentor: busy, a little skeptical, and pleased when you have clearly read the data.
- They only know what has happened so far. Nobody at Soony knows what comes next.
- They don't speak for suppliers. To get something from a supplier, write to the supplier.
- Talking doesn't change the data. Telling them what to do is not the same as making it happen.

---

## 10. Judging

Lio judges "the way an investor and a customer would judge a young startup." No trick questions, no hidden metric, no hidden test set or secret evaluation data. Judging weighs the strength of the logic, the problem-solving approach, the idea, the prototype and the presentation more than heavy coding.

### Entry ticket (required to be judged)
- The system runs **live in front of the jury**.
- A working prototype (**deployed** if possible).
- Pitch deck (the slides you present).
- Demo video, **3 minutes max**.
- Repo (e.g. GitHub) with a short README.
- **Submission deadline: Sunday 22 Nov, 12:00.**

### Four criteria

**1. A pitch that sticks.** A clear story from problem to solution to impact. "Five teams later, the jury should still remember yours."
- Do we understand the problem in the first 30 seconds?
- Is there a clear line from what hurts at Soony to what you built?
- Did you use what you learned from Soony's team, not just from the data?
- Strong: a story with a real moment in it ("On Saturday, Felix told us… so we built…"). Weak: a feature tour, or ten slides of architecture before anyone knows why it matters.

**2. A real business case.** Why this, why now, what is it worth? "Soony is your first customer, not your only one."
- Is it well motivated: why this problem, why now, what is it worth in money or time?
- Why would Soony pay for it, and roughly how much?
- Who else has this problem? Does it work beyond one game launch?
- Strong: a number the customer cares about, and a clear path to the next ten customers. Weak: "The market is huge," or a solution that only works for this one weekend.

**3. Technical depth.** Agents do real work on messy, changing data, and nothing is hardcoded.
- Do the agents take real actions (decide, write, escalate), or only summarise?
- Is there a solid architecture (tool use, reasoning, state), not one big prompt?
- How is messy and contradictory data handled? Is anything hardcoded?
- When a new drop arrives, does the system cope, or does it need rebuilding?
- Strong: agents that take real actions on the messy data, and a team that can explain what happens when the system gets something wrong. Weak: a chat window around one prompt, or values copied from the data into the code.

**4. Taste.** Does it look and feel like a real product? "Soony's team has ten minutes and forty dashboards."
- Does it look and feel like a real product?
- Is it all of a piece: one design language, a clear layout, nothing bolted on?
- Would the people you interviewed use it on a stressful Sunday?
- Are the small details right: wording, defaults, the moment a human has to decide?
- Strong: one product with a clean, consistent design, a clear recommendation and one click to act. Weak: every number on one screen, mixed styles and default components, leaving the user to figure out what to do.

Plus: **a live demo on real data. Not optional.**

### Demo format
- Demos are on **Sunday from 14:00**.
- **3 minutes of pitch on stage, then 2 minutes of jury questions.**
  1. **The problem**: what hurts at Soony, and what you learned by asking.
  2. **Your system**: agents at work on real customer data, live.
  3. **The business**: why Soony pays for it, and who else would.
- Jury tips: "Show, don't tell. Start the demo early. Slides are support, not the show." "Have a backup. If the Wi-Fi dies, your demo video saves you. Still, the live run is what counts." "Go deep, not wide. One problem solved properly beats a tour of everything."

---

## 11. Timeline

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Sat 21 Nov, morning | Kickoff (about 50 hours before launch) |
| Sat 06:00–22:00 | Soony packing shift 1 |
| Sat afternoon | Office hours, Block A (portal: 15:00) |
| Sat 17:00 | Office hours, Block B |
| Night | No data drops ("sleep-friendly") |
| Sun 06:00–20:00 | Soony packing shift 2 |
| Sun 09:00 | Office hours, Block C |
| **Sun 12:00** | **Submission deadline** |
| Sun 14:00 | Demos |
| Sun 20:00 | Grand Heist 6 launches, trucks leave Hamburg |

---

## 12. Prize and fine print

- Prize: **a PS5 and GTA 6 for every member of the winning team.** "If Soony doesn't launch on time… neither do you."
- Use the data only for this hackathon. Do not share it outside the team.
- Hardware is optional. Questions go to Discord or the Lio booth.

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, others) working in this repo.

## What this is

Our entry for the Lio challenge "Keep the Line Running" at START Hack Munich 2026.

- Fictional customer: Soony, a games publisher launching Grand Heist 6 on Sun 22 Nov, 20:00
- Everything is packed in one distribution center in Hamburg; six suppliers deliver the parts
- Still open at kickoff: 128,000 Standard Editions (4 parts each) and 25,200 numbered Collector's Editions (7 parts each)
- Packing time left: Sat 06:00 to 22:00, Sun 06:00 to 20:00

The product idea is not fixed yet. Check the README and recent commits for the current direction.

## The rules that shape the code

- **Agents do real work.** They read, decide and act: write to suppliers, open decisions, escalate. A dashboard on top of a spreadsheet is not enough.
- **Nothing hardcoded.** Never copy values from the data into code. Everything is derived from the portal data at runtime.
- **The data changes.** New files land in the portal during the hack, unannounced. Code must handle new and changed files without a rebuild.
- **The data is messy on purpose.** Expect contradictions, missing values, scans and four languages (KR, CN, PL, EN). Surface contradictions instead of silently picking one side.
- **Confidential.** Use the data only for this hackathon and never share it outside the team. Do not commit portal data (`data/` is gitignored); fetch it through the API.

## Data access

- Customer portal: `https://start-hack-portal-cxh3crbdaef2f8gt.westeurope-01.azurewebsites.net`
- API (team token from the portal's Settings): `GET /api/v1/files`, `GET /api/v1/files/{path}`, `GET /api/v1/archive.zip`, `GET /api/v1/openapi.json`
- Token and other secrets go in `.env` (gitignored), never in code or commits
- Supplier email only gets answers from sender addresses registered in the portal's Settings

## Deadlines

- **Sun 12:00:** hand-in: deployed prototype, pitch deck, demo video (max 3 min), this repo with a short README
- **Sun 14:00:** live demo, 3 min pitch plus 2 min questions

Prefer working, deployed and demoable over complete. Go deep on one problem.

## Team workflow

Who is doing what lives in `PROGRESS.md` at the repo root. Humans and agents follow the same steps.

- **Before starting:** `git pull --rebase`, read `PROGRESS.md`, add or update your line under **Now** (`- <name>: <task>`), then commit and push that change right away so others see it
- **Don't take work someone else is on.** If your task touches files another person's **Now** line covers, talk to them first
- **While working:** small commits, one topic each; `git pull --rebase` before every `git push`; push at least every hour
- **When done:** move your line to **Done** with the date, note any decision under **Decisions** and any blocker under **Blockers**, then push
- **Conflicts in `PROGRESS.md`:** keep both sides; edit only your own line
- Agents: do the above on behalf of the person you work for, using their name

## Entire (session tracking)

Entire records agent sessions as checkpoints and links them to commits.

- Hooks for Claude Code (`.claude/settings.json`) and Codex (`.codex/hooks.json`) are committed; they do nothing if `entire` is not installed
- Checkpoints upload to this (private) repo on `git push`

### Setup (once per clone)

1. Install the CLI. macOS: `brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire`. Other systems: see https://docs.entire.io/cli/installation
2. Check it runs: `entire --version`
3. In your clone, install the git hooks (they link commits to checkpoints and upload them on push):

   ```bash
   entire enable --agent claude-code --local --telemetry=false
   entire agent add codex    # only if you use Codex
   ```

   `--local` writes your choices to `.entire/settings.local.json`, so the shared `.entire/settings.json` stays unchanged. Drop `--telemetry=false` if you don't mind anonymous usage stats.
4. **Restart your agents:** quit every Claude Code or Codex session that was open in this repo and start a new one. Hooks load when a session starts, so sessions that were already running are not tracked
5. Codex only: in the new session, open `/hooks` and approve the Entire hooks
6. Verify: `entire status` should show `Enabled`, your agents, `Checkpoints sync to: origin` and `Secret scanners · betterleaks, goredact`
7. If `entire enable` changed `.claude/settings.json` or `.codex/hooks.json`, check `git diff` before committing; the committed versions already work for everyone

`entire doctor` diagnoses and fixes stuck sessions.
- Shared redaction settings (PII, betterleaks, goredact) live in `.entire/settings.json`; personal settings go in `.entire/settings.local.json` (gitignored)
- Redaction is best effort: never paste secrets into agent sessions

## Entire Brain (shared team memory)

Brain distills agent sessions into durable memories and syncs them across the team. Agents read `.entire/agent-guide.md` (linked from `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`) for how to use it.

### Setup (once per clone, after the Entire setup above)

1. The CLI must be 0.11.6 or newer: `entire --version`. Upgrade with `brew upgrade --cask entire`. If an older `entire` sits earlier on your `PATH` (e.g. `~/.local/bin`), remove it
2. Install the plugins:

   ```bash
   entire plugin install brain
   entire plugin install graph
   ```

3. In your clone, build the brain and connect it to the team's hosted memory set:

   ```bash
   entire brain setup
   entire brain connect
   ```

   `setup` also installs a background watcher that refreshes the brain every 5 minutes. It refuses to index a dirty working tree, so commit or stash first
4. Restart your agents, as above
5. Verify: `entire brain status` should show `Daemon | running` and `Brainstore | connected`
6. If `entire brain setup` changed `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/settings.json`, check `git diff`; the committed versions already work for everyone

## Conventions

- Commit subjects in imperative mood, at most 50 characters; details as bullets in the body
- One commit per topic
- Keep secrets, tokens and personal data out of code, fixtures and commit messages

Every version also lands in the version store (`data/store/`, see below). All of `data/` is gitignored: the data is confidential.
+A fixed loop polls the portal, keeps every file version and lets an LLM agent analyse each change.

+1. **Poll** `GET /api/v1/files` and compare SHA-256 checksums. New or replaced files are downloaded (the first sync uses `archive.zip`) and stored by checksum under `data/store/blobs/`; nothing is overwritten.
+2. **Log** every version, poll, analysis and finding in SQLite (`data/store/ask-soony.db`), so each finding points at the exact file version behind it.

+3. **Analyse** each new or changed file with an agent. +The first poll stores the current state as a baseline without analysing it; only later changes are analysed. `analyze --path <prefix>` queues existing files on purpose.

lines: +- When strategizing do not change existing code files, pure brainstorming.
+- For independent analysis, you can write and run your own code, without interfering with existing codebase.
+- Do not implement code yourself, tell me what to implement in chat.
+Soony's own data (`soony/`). Supplier data: `inconsistencies_suppliers.md` (P…). Each row compares what the system says with what the evidence says.

+| S1 | Art books: SAP stock 80,000 (batch 5000413065, "over delivery accepted") | Delivery note `receiving/DC-HAM/20261118_WZ-261116-473.jpg`: 80,000 crossed out, 8,000 handwritten. PO 4500318768/3 is for 8,000. | **About 5,900 short** (plan says "ok"). Fix: Karton has 8,000 in stock (P6). |

+| S2 | Statue lot 5000413063 (5,600) is "unrestricted" | `inspection_report_5000413063.pdf`: 9 of 125 defective, limit 3 | **About 3,400 short** (plan says "ok"). A concession needs the vacant Category Lead (S15). |

+| S4 | Launch plan counts 48,000 game cards by air, arriving Sat 21 Nov (SHP-2026-04311) | Shipping advice: 28,000 flew; 20,000 arrive Tue 24 Nov (P2). The standard route (S5) also points to Mon 23 Nov. | **About 6,800 short.** 34,800 short if the 28,000 miss Sun 20:00. |
+| S3 | BOM: 4 magnets per Collector's Edition, stock 0. The plan shows "CHECK" for 100,800. | PackRight contract Annex A: magnets come fitted in the box (P1) | **False alarm.** |
+| S6 | Excel tracker: 14 shipments | Shipment feed: 25 | The tracker misses both game card air shipments. |
+| S7 | Tracker: SHP-2026-04276 "in transit" | Feed: arrived at port, available for pick-up | 350,000 game card cases waiting at the Hamburg terminal |
+| S9 | Plan dated Fri 20 Nov 18:00 | Packing log ends Thu 19 Nov | Friday's output is missing. *To verify.* |
+| S13 | 78,000 "Pre-order Pin GH6" booked as misc merchandise | No PO, not in master data, not in the BOM | Unordered goods from Dongguan (P20) |
+- **S8** The shipment feed has no quantities, only PO numbers. Quantities have to be inferred from the POs.
+- **S10** Stock is "not counted": physical counts are 4 to 19 days old.
+- **S14** Only 69 of 392 receipts have a scanned delivery note, all from Sep 2026 onward.
+- **S11** GH5 uses the same case and leaflet as GH6, but the plan counts GH6 only. Low risk (large surplus).
+- **S12** Criticality flags are unreliable: the statue, steel case and Collector's box are not marked critical.
+- **S15** The Category Lead for Collector's Items is vacant. Concessions, Collector's air freight and supplier releases escalate to the Head of Procurement (PP-07 §6).
+- **S16** Two Pune statue orders are stuck in "awaiting approval" because the conditional release expired (P17).
+- Two PO exports with different layouts. The legacy one uses `;`, decimal commas, `MM/DD/YYYY` dates, numeric supplier ids (`19` = `SUP-0019`) and no currency column.
+- Routes go via SGSIN, which is missing from `master/ports.csv`.
+- The tracker uses supplier names; the ERP uses supplier ids.
+- Check the other 57 delivery-note scans for handwritten corrections like S1. This is the verifier's first job.
+Supplier data (`suppliers/`). Soony data: `inconsistencies_soony.md` (S…). All 229 supplier PDFs were read, and every confirmation was checked line by line against SAP.

+| P2 | Feed and plan: 48,000 Hwaseong game cards arrive 21 Nov (SHP-2026-04311) | `Shipping_advice_020-48113256_4500318735.pdf` (appeared 21 Nov): 28,000 flew, 20,000 arrive Tue 24 Nov | **About 6,800 game cards short** (S4). Late delivery qualifies for LTA §7 damages of about $3.9k/week. |

+| P3 | Master data: GH6 sleeve rev. B | Karton confirmations print rev. C ("received from Soony Marketing 2026-08-07"); PackRight prints rev. B | Hamburg holds 122,000 rev. C and 64,000 rev. B sleeves. **If only rev. B is valid: about 64,000 short.** |

+| P4 | Nothing (no capacity limit anywhere) | Polish notice dated 9 Nov: Karton's offset printing and bindery are down Sat 14:00 to Mon 06:00 | No reprints before launch. Karton's rush offer (P5) contradicts this notice, and rush printing lands too late anyway. |
+| P6 | Nothing | Karton offer of 21 Nov: 8,000 art books from stock, loaded in 4 h, plus about 9 h by truck | **Fixes S1.** €16,800, so a buyer can approve it. Expires 22 Nov. Needs a dock slot. |
+| P16 | Profile: Pune `conditional`, release expired 30 Oct | All Pune confirmations claim "approved for serial supply" | Explains why the failed lot was booked as usable (S2) |

+| P13 | Feed: Boise SHP-2026-04314 "booked" for 21 Nov. SAP: DDP Hamburg | Confirmation for PO 4500318769: on hold until Soony confirms EXW in writing. The contract says EXW. | 36,000 cards stuck. After launch anyway. Fix: one email. |
+| P1 | BOM: magnets are a separate part, stock 0 | PackRight contract Annex A: fitted in the Collector's box | **False alarm** (S3) |

+- **P12, P15, P7** Order lines with no supplier confirmation: Hwaseong 5, Boise 7, Karton 2 POs, PackRight 3. Boise's unconfirmed line is on a plane (SHP-2026-04310). Karton's unconfirmed PO has a truck booked (SHP-2026-04316).
+- **P10** Hwaseong PO 4500318636: SAP promises 26 May, the confirmation says 9 Jun.

+| P9 | Hwaseong | GH5 card fixed at $5.40 until expiry | Confirmations quote $5.51 to $5.62 (SAP keeps $5.40) |

content.text:
I merged Farhan's PR #1 into `main` with both fixes and pushed it as `2d8868f`. GitHub now shows the PR as merged.

**What came in from Farhan:**
- A data-analysis notebook and a `requirements.txt` for it.
- `inconsistencies_soony.md` and `inconsistencies_suppliers.md`, which list contradictions he found in the data.
- `questions.md`, ranked questions to put to Soony's team in office hours.
- `strategy.md`.
- `challenge_docs/`, the original Lio PDFs and slides (about 27 MB).
- Two Claude commands, `/strategize` and `/tell_me`.

**The two fixes, both in the merge commit:**
- I kept `.env.example`. His last commit had deleted it, and josteng's portal watcher reads its settings from that file.
- I cleared the notebook's outputs, so the code is there but no portal data is printed in the file. Re-run it locally to see the results.

**Also new from josteng since earlier:** a portal watcher with an LLM analysis agent, and a command to download the portal data in one go.

The notebook's outputs are still in Farhan's earlier commits, so anyone who looks back through the git history can see them. The repo is private, so I'd leave that as it is rather than rewrite shared history.

Farhan and josteng should both run `git pull`.
